title: What are Union Types?
overview: Union types allow a variable to store more than one possible type. They are created using the pipe (|) operator.

example.title: Union Type Example

title: Using Union Types in Functions
overview: Union types can be used in function parameters when a function should accept multiple types of values.

title: Type Narrowing
overview: Type narrowing allows TypeScript to determine the exact type of a union value before performing operations on it.

example.title: Type Narrowing Example

title: What are Intersection Types?
overview: Intersection types combine multiple types into one. A value must contain all properties from the combined types.

example.title: Intersection Example

title: Union vs Intersection Types
overview: Union types allow multiple possible types, while intersection types combine multiple types into a single type.

example.title: Comparison
example.content:
Union:
string | number
(One of these types)

Intersection:
User & Admin
(Both types together)

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how union and intersection types work, how to handle multiple types, narrow values, and combine custom types in TypeScript.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Union uses | operator.
✔ Allows multiple possible types.
✔ Intersection uses & operator.
✔ Combines multiple types together.
